topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and cellular conditions of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable clonal evolution when the affected cells and their microenvironment permit it.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the interpretation of causal evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and how that contribution is understood through competing explanations and epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and cancer-producing cellular changes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage capable of generating cancer-associated mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on the exposed tissue and its developmental state, concluding with a recap of the mechanisms underlying that susceptibility.

topics.label: Mutational signatures as evidence of carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how patterns in cancer genomes can be used to infer exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the available approaches to testing carcinogenic potential and the limitations of the evidence each approach provides.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
